judgments.reason: The passage establishes an Accessory Dwelling Unit Trust Fund supporting property owners with incomes not more than 110 percent of median income to build an ADU, matching the claim.
The passage states funds may be in the form of grants, loans or other financial assistance.
The passage lists pre-development and non-recurring closing costs including design, site preparation, utility connection fees, impact fees and permitting fees.
The passage expressly names low and no interest loans, grants, subsidies, and credit enhancements.
The passage requires assistance to be the minimum amount necessary to make a project feasible.
The passage says the fund is administered by the Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities or through contracts with one or more administering agencies.
The passage permits subcontracts with non-profit organizations established pursuant to chapter 180.
The passage credits the fund with appropriations specifically designated for it, gifts, grants, contributions, and loan repayments.
The passage states year-end money does not revert to the General Fund, which is what remaining in the fund means.
The passage describes a property owner with income up to 110% of area median income as defined by HUD.
The passage describes exactly this income threshold for a property owner, and the claim hedges with "could count."
The passage states funds may go to eligible participants as grants, loans or other financial assistance to build an accessory dwelling unit.
